question: What was the average duty of a low-pressure Watt engine?
answer: [1] Watt's original low-pressure designs were able to deliver duty as high as 25 million, but averaged about 17.

sources.excerpt: er Newcomen designs. Duty is the number of foot-pounds of work delivered by burning one bushel (94 pounds) of coal. The best examples of Newcomen designs had a duty of about 7 million, but most were closer to 5 million. Watt's original low-pressure designs were able to deliver duty as high as 25 million, but averaged about 17. This was a three-fold improvement over the average Newcomen design. Early Watt engines equipped with high-pressure steam improved this to 65 million.
